brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.requirement: At least three bins to hold spices
requirements.evidence: Three full-depth bins: bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,-1,0.
Two keyhole hangers, accessory:0#-1,0#2 and accessory:0#1,-1#2, on the flat back faces of the two outer bases. How much weight they hold was not checked.

requirements.requirement: Shown as a spice rack (spice jars in the bins)
requirements.evidence: This was my own addition, not part of your brief. The prop catalogue has no spice jars or anything like them, so I put no props in the bins.

finish.summary: I built a spice rack from three full hex bases with a full-depth bin in each, and it hangs from two keyhole hangers. Neighbouring hex cells never have outer faces in one flat plane. So the bases are set in a zigzag: the two outer ones, at (-1,0) and (1,-1), line up flat against the wall and each carries a keyhole hanger on its back face (slot 2). The middle one, at (0,0), sits slightly forward and is bolted to both of them. I worked the wall-facing side out from the hex grid layout because the picture tool returned no image. Please check that the hangers end up on the back, against the wall, before you print. I added solid end caps on the open faces and bolted the joints. That makes 20 printed parts, about 1,557 g of filament and roughly 36 hours of printing. The configurator's checks found no rule problems and no colliding parts. It checks fit only: whether the plastic and the wall screws can hold a full rack is not checked.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
